text:
alex chen: Heads up — we're seeing a big tail-latency spike on prod around 03:12 UTC. 99th pct for /v1/generate jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s. Any recent deploys?
priya rao: no deploys around that time from our side. I see a bunch of scale-ups from the autoscaler though.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: started scale-up for pool 'inference-prod-g4' at 2026-03-18T03:11:48Z — target 6 -> 10 instances. provisioning: queued.
samir patel: logs show node startup lingered ~95s for the new instances. infra-monitor, can you share provisioning traces?
infra-monitor: attached: provisioning trace snippet:
```
2026-03-18T03:11:50Z instance-089 boot -> kernel-module matmul_v2 loaded
2026-03-18T03:12:20Z instance-089 nvml ready
2026-03-18T03:13:25Z instance-089 model-runtime started
2026-03-18T03:13:45Z instance-089 registered -> ready for routing
```
meanwhile instance-092 had fallback kernel selection at runtime.
emma li: @samir can you pull perf profile from the cold instances? curious if kernel fallback caused high CPU or contention with existing tenants.
samir patel: pasted a perf summary from instance-092 (cold):
```
# perf top snapshot
- matmul_generic_kernel 48.2% (hot)
- kernel_selector 18.5%
- kv_cache_lock 9.1%
- python_gil 7.3%
- network_poll 5.0%
```
that matmul_generic is our slow/generic fallback. should be using matmul_v2 optimized kernels.
priya rao: why did kernel_selector pick generic? model signature matches. config shows quantization profile 'q4_0' for that model. recent change to prefer generic when memory pressure > 72%?
emma li: I remember a heuristic change last week: if peak GPU memory > 70% use the generic kernel to reduce mem fragmentation. that could cause orders-of-magnitude slower matmuls.
alex chen: so chain of events: autoscaler launches new cold instances -> during warmup memory pressure + co-located containers -> kernel selector flips to generic -> generated responses on those instances much slower -> routing still sends some % of traffic -> tail latency spikes.
priya rao: also noticed KV cache warmup behavior: the first requests miss the cache and trigger synchronous fetches that hold a cache lock. combined with slower kernels that increases queueing.
samir patel: here's a snippet from runtime logs showing KV contention + kernel fallback for one request:
```
[03:13:33.122] request=start id=0x7fae path=/v1/generate
[03:13:33.200] kv_cache: miss key=prefix-abc acquiring lock
[03:13:33.205] kernel_selector: selected=matmul_generic reason=mem_pressure
[03:13:34.900] kv_cache: populate done
[03:13:35.120] request=finish latency=1.998s
```
priya rao: that sequence explains the ~2s tail. Good catch.
emma li: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable the aggressive mem-pressure->generic fallback for a short window, 2) have autoscaler wait for instance 'ready' + KV_cache_preload job before routing, 3) increase warm-pool minimum to avoid scale-ups under load.
alex chen: short-term: flip the fallback boolean in config to false for prod canary, and add a quick prewarm job to populate KV prefixes for popular routes. can devops push a toggle?
infra-monitor: created toggle: `runtime.kernel_selector.force_optimized=false` -> setting applied to canary at 03:22 UTC. also scheduled KV prewarm job for top-100 prefixes.
samir patel: after the toggle we saw 99p drop back to ~260ms within two minutes. autoscaler provisioning still slow but routing to cold instances no longer produces slow kernels.
priya rao: longer-term: we should update the kernel selection heuristic to consider instance age and current instance-local eviction metrics rather than a blunt mem% cutoff. also make KV prewarm as opt-in for pools.
emma li: filing a follow-up perf task: PROJ-INF-456: 'kernel selector age-aware policy + KV prewarm handshake' — will include benchmarks and rollback tests.
alex chen: thanks everyone. summary: root cause = kernel fallback triggered by mem-pressure heuristic on cold instances + KV cache misses causing lock contention. mitigation = revert heuristic and prewarm KV; long-term = smarter selector + autoscaler/warm-pool changes. :thumbsup:
priya rao: noted, will drive the change and schedule rollout plan.
deploy-bot: incident note auto-created: INC-2026-03-18-02 — prod tail-latency spike resolved by runtime config toggle.
emma li: adding retrospective: include perf regression tests for kernel_selector logic in our CI so heuristics are exercised under simulated warm/cold mixes.
alex chen: cool — closing the loop, please add any missing context to the incident doc.
